claims.text: NbMoTaW HEA is suitable for lattice heat-conductivity applications.
NbMoTaW HEA has a high melting point.
The high melting point makes NbMoTaW suitable for lattice heat conductivity.
NbMoTaW HEA has potential for reduced phonon scattering.
NbMoTaW HEA can be manufactured using selective laser melting.
The proposed use or processing occurs under high-temperature conditions.
SRO precipitates scatter phonons in NbMoTaW HEA.
The proposed process produces reduced phonon-scattering times.
Lattice distortion participates in the thermal-transport mechanism.
SLM-manufactured NbMoTaW HEA will have decreased thermal conductivity.
Traditional thermal forming and casting methods are the baseline comparator.
Processing NbMoTaW by traditional casting is limited by available equipment temperature.
Further study of the mechanical properties of SLM-fabricated NbMoTaW is necessary.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing thermal conductivity and phonon-scattering rates between SLM-manufactured and traditionally manufactured NbMoTaW.
Failure of the SLM material to show decreased thermal conductivity relative to the traditional-method comparator would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis invokes reduced phonon scattering, whereas the mechanism invokes reduced scattering times, which ordinarily indicates stronger or more frequent scattering. The latter coheres with decreased thermal conductivity, but the former points in the opposite direction unless 'phonon scattering reduction' was intended to mean reduction of scattering time.
